text:
samir: CI red on macOS after yesterday's toolchain image roll. many targets failing with <filesystem> not found. failing shard: macos-x86_64-2 (kokoro). build log excerpt:
```
external/com_googlesource_code_repos_gcc/include/c++/v1/filesystem:37:10: fatal error: 'filesystem' file not found
#include <filesystem>
         ^~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.

Target //libs/storage:storage_lib failed to build
```

lina: @samir thanks for the ping. did the roll change libc++ vs libstdc++? that header is from C++17 lib. :eyes:

ben: I saw a blurb in the infra PR that the image bumped to macos-clang-14 + SDK 12. Maybe the stdlib headers moved. can you paste the kokoro job link?

samir: https://kokoro.internal/build/12345 (private) — job logs linked. also happens on local dev mac VM when I swap to the new toolchain image image://macos-clang-14:latest

alex: quick triage checklist: 1) verify include paths the compiler sees 2) try `clang++ -v -E -x c++ /dev/null` inside the image 3) bazel clean --expunge and a full rebuild 4) confirm symlinks in /usr/include or toolchain sysroot

katie: re: include paths — when the image switched we had a change that sets -stdlib=libc++ explicitly in the toolchain wrapper. if some code expects libstdc++ headers, that could hide <filesystem>. But generally <filesystem> lives in libc++. weird.

samir: ran a local repro in the image. `clang++ --version` shows Apple clang 14, but `clang++ -E -x c++ - < /dev/null` output shows include dirs: /usr/local/include then a path that doesn't contain c++/v1. So looks like SDK layout changed.

ben: can you paste the BUILD rule for the failing target? if it's using cc_library with system_includes or a custom include path it might shadow the stdlib headers.

samir: BUILD: `cc_library(name = "storage_lib", srcs = [...], deps = ["//libs/fs:fs_wrapper"])` — no special flags. fs_wrapper includes a wrapper header that does `#include <filesystem>` unchanged.

lina: @samir can you try adding this to the bazel invocation to see which header is picked up? `bazel build //libs/storage:storage_lib --sandbox_debug --spawn_strategy=standalone --cxxopt="-v"` and paste the preprocessor include trace.

samir: ran that, preprocessor trace shows it searching in `/Applications/Xcode_12.4.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX12.sdk/usr/include` but I don't see c++/v1 path. looks like the SDK in the image is missing libc++ headers.

tj: Could be that the toolchain image intended to bundle libc++ into a different path (e.g., llvm/lib/clang/14/include/c++/v1) and our wrapper isn't pointing to it. Check the wrapper script that sets --sysroot or -isystem flags.

alex: Good call. Also check the bazel CROSSTOOL / toolchain definition we supply for macos. If it hardcodes SDK paths, an SDK bump can break it.

katie: I found the infra PR: infra/rolls#679. It updates the image but forgot to add an extra symlink to /usr/include/c++/v1. cc @infra-team.

samir: ok, what's the fastest mitigation? revert the image? add a fallback include path? request kokoro rerun of pre-commit?

lina: short-term: add a patch to our macos toolchain wrapper that adds `-isystem /opt/llvm/include/c++/v1` if present, and run a tryjob. longer-term: infra should fix the image.

ben: I can upload a tiny tryjob patch and trigger kokoro. Samir, can you confirm the exact path in the image where c++/v1 lives?

samir: path is `/usr/local/llvm-14/lib/clang/14.0.0/include/c++/v1` in the image. adding `-isystem /usr/local/llvm-14/lib/clang/14.0.0/include` fixes the build locally.

ci-bot: Re-run requested by @ben for job macos-x86_64-2 (kokoro). job: kokoro/internal/try/98765

ben: kicked the tryjob. if it passes we'll land a short-lived fallback flag while infra fixes the image. @infra-team please prioritize the image symlink fix.

lina: also adding note to the toolchain docs that SDK bumps require verifying that libc++ headers remain reachable by the wrapper. I'll open a doc PR.

alex: procedure note: if we need to bisect the toolchain image roll, we can `git bisect` the infra roll PRs, but since this is an image artifact it's faster to fix the wrapper and then revert later if needed.

samir: tryjob passed on the patched wrapper. I'll prepare a small CL that inserts the `-isystem` only when the path exists and mark it as temporary. CL: https://phabricator.redwood/CL/2910 (private)

katie: thanks. once CL lands let's rerun the full macos presubmit matrix. also please add the failure logs to the release notes for the roll so we don't regress. :thumbsup:

tj: FYI I added a quick Nagios alert to the infra roll playbook to validate `c++/v1` presence automatically on future image builds.

samir: awesome — thanks everyone. closing the loop here once infra confirms image fix. :white_check_mark:
